title: GEO vs SEO: What's the Difference, and Do UK Small Businesses Need Both? (2026)
meta_title: GEO vs SEO: What's the Difference? UK Guide 2026
meta_description: SEO gets you clicks from Google. GEO gets you named by ChatGPT and Gemini. What each does, costs, and how UK small businesses should split their budget.
keywords: do i need geo and seo

faq.q: What is the difference between GEO and SEO?
faq.a: SEO helps your website rank in Google and Bing results so people click through. GEO helps your business get named inside AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity.
Not usually, in 2026. GEO now most often means generative engine optimisation for AI search. Optimising for a location is normally called local SEO.
No. AI assistants often draw on pages that already rank well, so strong SEO supports GEO. Most businesses need both, and around 70% of the work is shared.

faq.q: Should a small business start with SEO or GEO?
faq.a: Start with the shared foundations: crawler access, structured data and answer-first pages. Local businesses then lean on SEO and Google Business Profile; online and professional services should add GEO early.

faq.q: How do I measure GEO results?
faq.a: Track a list of the questions your customers ask, across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity, and record how often each one names your business compared with competitors.

faq.q: How much does GEO and SEO cost in the UK?
faq.a: Combined plans for small businesses typically cost £89 to £400 a month. Agency retainers cost about £1,100 to £3,800 a month. See our full UK price guide for details.
